organic_advantages: Builds soil organic carbon and living soil biology (earthworms, mycorrhiza, beneficial microbes) instead of depleting them; chemical NPK and pesticides erode this over time.
Lower input cost: most remedies are made from farm resources (dung, urine, neem, leaves, ash), cutting cash spent on agro-chemicals and reducing debt risk.
Improves water-holding capacity of soil, so crops cope better with dry spells - a direct climate-resilience gain.
No pesticide residues on produce or in water; safer for the farmer, family, livestock, pollinators and natural enemies of pests.
Pests rarely develop resistance to neem, microbes and traps the way they do to single-molecule chemicals, so control lasts.
Access to premium markets, organic certification (NPOP in India) and government support such as PKVY / Namami Gange organic clusters.
Chemical fixes act fast but treat only the symptom and can worsen the problem (pest resurgence, soil acidification, nutrient imbalance); organic methods correct the cause.
disclaimer: AI-assisted diagnosis is a guide, not a certified diagnosis. For severe or spreading problems confirm with your Krishi Vigyan Kendra / local extension officer, and follow your organic certifier's list of permitted inputs.

def_nitrogen.name: Nitrogen deficiency
symptoms: Older (lower) leaves turn uniformly pale yellow first

organic_remedies.name: Jeevamrut / Ghanajeevamrut
organic_remedies.prepare: Ferment 10 kg cow dung, 10 L cow urine, 2 kg jaggery, 2 kg pulse flour and a handful of bund soil in 200 L water for 5-7 days, stirring twice daily.
organic_remedies.apply: Drench 200 L/acre through irrigation or spray filtered 10% solution every 15 days.
organic_remedies.timing: Repeat 2-3 times in the vegetative stage

organic_remedies.name: Well-decomposed compost / vermicompost
organic_remedies.prepare: Compost farm residue and dung for 60-90 days.
organic_remedies.apply: 2-4 t/acre worked into soil before sowing; side-dress 500 kg/acre.
organic_remedies.timing: Before sowing and at first weeding

organic_remedies.name: Green manure / legume intercrop
organic_remedies.apply: Incorporate at 45 days / flowering, 2-3 weeks before the main crop.

preventive: Avoid over-tillage that burns organic matter
def_nitrogen.chemical_comparison: Urea gives a quick green-up but loses 30-50% to leaching/volatilisation, acidifies soil and adds to greenhouse gas (N2O).

def_phosphorus.name: Phosphorus deficiency
symptoms: Dark green or purplish/reddish leaves and stems
Slow root development and delayed flowering

organic_remedies.name: Rock phosphate + compost
organic_remedies.prepare: Mix 50 kg rock phosphate with 1 t compost and keep moist for 3-4 weeks.
organic_remedies.apply: Broadcast 1 t of enriched compost per acre.

organic_remedies.name: Phosphate-solubilising bacteria (PSB) biofertiliser
organic_remedies.prepare: Buy certified culture from KVK/agri-input store.
organic_remedies.apply: Seed treatment 5-10 g/kg seed or 1 kg/acre mixed in compost.

preventive: Maintain soil pH 6-7 (P is locked in acid/alkaline soils)
def_phosphorus.chemical_comparison: DAP/SSP are quickly fixed in soil (only 15-20% used by the crop) and build up cadmium/fluoride over time.

def_potassium.name: Potassium deficiency
symptoms: Yellowing then browning/scorching of leaf margins, starting on older leaves

organic_remedies.name: Wood ash
organic_remedies.prepare: Use clean ash from untreated wood/crop residue.
organic_remedies.apply: 50-100 kg/acre incorporated into soil; avoid on alkaline soils.

organic_remedies.name: Banana-peel / plant-ash tea
organic_remedies.prepare: Soak 1 kg banana peel or 1 kg ash in 10 L water for 2-3 days.

organic_remedies.name: Composted crop residue, banana stem/farm compost

preventive: Return crop residue to the soil
def_potassium.chemical_comparison: Muriate of potash adds chloride and salt stress; repeated use can harm salt-sensitive crops and soil structure.

def_iron.name: Iron deficiency (chlorosis)
symptoms: Young (top) leaves yellow with veins staying green
In severe cases whole young leaves turn white

organic_remedies.name: Compost/FYM enriched with iron-rich material
organic_remedies.prepare: Compost with iron-rich clay or old iron filings (untreated).

organic_remedies.name: Vermiwash / compost-tea foliar spray
organic_remedies.prepare: Collect vermiwash from the vermicompost unit; dilute 1:10.

organic_remedies.name: Ferrous sulphate with FYM (only if permitted by your certifier)
organic_remedies.prepare: Mix 5 kg ferrous sulphate with 50 kg FYM.
organic_remedies.timing: At first symptom, on soil-test confirmation

preventive: Lower soil pH with organic matter/sulphur-rich compost
def_iron.chemical_comparison: Synthetic chelates (e.g. Fe-EDDHA) are costly and washed out; compost restores iron availability by acidifying the root zone.

def_zinc.name: Zinc deficiency
symptoms: Interveinal chlorosis / bronzing on young leaves

organic_remedies.name: Compost + zinc-rich farm amendments
organic_remedies.prepare: Compost with leaf litter, sesame/mustard cake and cow dung.

organic_remedies.name: Zinc sulphate (where permitted after soil test)
organic_remedies.prepare: Mineral input allowed by many organic standards on proven deficiency.

organic_remedies.name: Zinc-solubilising biofertiliser
organic_remedies.apply: Seed or soil application per label.

def_zinc.chemical_comparison: Repeated high-dose zinc salts can accumulate; organic matter keeps zinc plant-available naturally.

def_magnesium.name: Magnesium deficiency
symptoms: Interveinal yellowing on older leaves with green veins

organic_remedies.name: Epsom salt foliar (permitted mineral, small dose)
organic_remedies.prepare: Dissolve 10 g magnesium sulphate per litre.
organic_remedies.timing: Once, repeat after 2 weeks if needed

def_magnesium.chemical_comparison: High-dose synthetic potash can lock out magnesium; balanced compost avoids this antagonism.

def_calcium.name: Calcium deficiency

organic_remedies.name: Gypsum / agricultural lime
organic_remedies.prepare: Powdered gypsum (neutral/alkaline soil) or lime (acid soil).

organic_remedies.name: Eggshell / shell-grit powder
organic_remedies.prepare: Dry and grind clean eggshells or oyster shells.
organic_remedies.apply: Mix into soil at planting hole (a handful/plant).

organic_remedies.name: Steady irrigation + mulch
organic_remedies.apply: Even soil moisture prevents calcium uptake failure.

def_calcium.chemical_comparison: Calcium-nitrate foliars are costly and add nitrogen; gypsum/organic matter fix the root-zone supply.

def_sulphur.name: Sulphur deficiency
symptoms: Uniform pale yellowing of young leaves (unlike nitrogen, starts on new growth)

organic_remedies.name: Elemental sulphur (permitted mineral)
organic_remedies.timing: Before sowing so soil microbes can oxidise it

preventive: Include oilseeds/onion only with sulphur supply
def_sulphur.chemical_comparison: Single super phosphate supplies S but also acidifies and adds P you may not need.

pest_aphids.name: Aphids
symptoms: Clusters of small soft insects on shoot tips and underside of leaves
Curled leaves, sticky honeydew, sooty mould

organic_remedies.name: Neem oil spray
organic_remedies.prepare: Mix 3-5 ml neem oil + 1 ml liquid soap per litre water.
organic_remedies.apply: Spray both leaf sides in the evening.

organic_remedies.name: Garlic-chilli extract
organic_remedies.prepare: Grind 50 g garlic + 50 g green chilli, soak in 1 L water overnight, filter, dilute to 10 L.

organic_remedies.name: Conserve natural enemies
organic_remedies.apply: Ladybird beetles, lacewings and hoverflies eat aphids.

pest_aphids.chemical_comparison: Broad-spectrum insecticides kill ladybirds and lacewings, so aphids rebound faster and resistance builds quickly.

pest_whitefly.name: Whitefly
symptoms: Tiny white flying insects when leaves are shaken

organic_remedies.name: Yellow sticky traps
organic_remedies.prepare: Yellow boards coated with grease/castor oil.

organic_remedies.name: Neem seed kernel extract (NSKE) 5%
organic_remedies.prepare: Crush 5 kg neem kernels, soak in 100 L water overnight, filter, add soap.

organic_remedies.name: Verticillium/Lecanicillium lecanii
organic_remedies.apply: 5 g/L water spray in humid weather.

pest_whitefly.chemical_comparison: Whiteflies quickly become resistant to synthetic insecticides; repeated sprays escalate cost.

pest_fall_armyworm.name: Fall armyworm
symptoms: Ragged holes and 'window-pane' feeding on young leaves
Sawdust-like frass in the whorl of maize/millet
Caterpillars with inverted Y on head

organic_remedies.name: Neem seed kernel extract 5% or neem oil 5 ml/L
organic_remedies.timing: At first sign; repeat after 7 days

organic_remedies.name: Pheromone traps + dry sand/ash in whorl
organic_remedies.apply: Drop a pinch of sand mixed with ash/lime in each whorl.

pest_fall_armyworm.chemical_comparison: Repeated sprays into the whorl are hard to time; they kill parasitoids and cost more than traps + biocontrol.

pest_stem_borer.name: Stem borer
symptoms: Entry holes and frass in stem

organic_remedies.name: Remove and destroy dead hearts; plough stubble

pest_stem_borer.chemical_comparison: Granular insecticides in standing water contaminate paddy ecosystems and kill fish/frogs that are natural pest predators.

pest_bollworm.name: Bollworm / fruit borer
symptoms: Holes in bolls, fruits or pods
pest_bollworm.chemical_comparison: Pyrethroid overuse triggered resistance and secondary pest outbreaks (whitefly, mealybug) in cotton.

pest_thrips.name: Thrips
symptoms: Silvery streaks and black dots on leaves

organic_remedies.name: Spinosad (permitted in organic systems)
organic_remedies.timing: Only if population is above threshold

pest_thrips.chemical_comparison: Thrips develop resistance rapidly to repeated synthetic sprays; traps and neem keep populations manageable.

pest_mealybug.name: Mealybug
symptoms: White cottony masses on stems, leaves and fruit

organic_remedies.name: Neem oil + soap wash
organic_remedies.prepare: 5 ml neem oil + 1 ml soap per litre.
organic_remedies.apply: Spray with force to penetrate wax.

pest_mealybug.chemical_comparison: Waxy coat shields mealybugs from most sprays, so chemicals need repeated heavy doses that also kill their predators.

pest_spider_mite.name: Red spider mite

organic_remedies.name: Forceful water spray
organic_remedies.apply: Wash leaf undersides to dislodge mites.

organic_remedies.name: Neem oil or wettable sulphur
organic_remedies.prepare: 5 ml neem oil/L or 2-3 g wettable sulphur/L.
organic_remedies.timing: Every 7 days; not sulphur in hot midday

pest_spider_mite.chemical_comparison: Acaricides quickly lose effect (rapid resistance) and kill predatory mites that otherwise hold populations down.

dis_powdery_mildew.name: Powdery mildew
symptoms: White powdery patches on leaves and stems

organic_remedies.name: Fermented buttermilk spray
organic_remedies.prepare: Dilute 1 L 3-day-old buttermilk in 10 L water.

organic_remedies.name: Wettable sulphur or baking-soda spray
organic_remedies.prepare: 3 g sulphur/L, or 5 g baking soda + 1 ml soap per L.
organic_remedies.apply: Spray in the cool of the day.

dis_powdery_mildew.chemical_comparison: Systemic fungicides can be needed only in severe outbreaks; repeated use breeds resistant strains.

dis_late_blight.name: Late blight (potato/tomato)
symptoms: White mould on leaf undersides in humid weather
Brown rot on tubers/fruit; rapid spread after rain

organic_remedies.name: Bordeaux mixture 1% (copper - restricted use in organic)
organic_remedies.prepare: Dissolve 1 kg copper sulphate and 1 kg fresh lime separately in 50 L each, then mix.
organic_remedies.apply: Spray before and during humid weather.
organic_remedies.timing: Every 7-10 days; check certifier limits on copper

preventive: Use resistant varieties and certified seed
Wide spacing and drip irrigation (dry foliage)
dis_late_blight.chemical_comparison: Systemic fungicides are used heavily in humid seasons and leave residues; resistance to metalaxyl is widespread.

dis_leaf_spot.name: Leaf spot / blight (fungal or bacterial)
symptoms: Brown or black circular spots with yellow halo
Spots merge, leaves dry and fall

organic_remedies.name: Pseudomonas fluorescens
organic_remedies.apply: 10 g/L foliar spray or 2.5 kg/acre with compost.

organic_remedies.name: Neem cake + compost
organic_remedies.prepare: Mix 100 kg neem cake per acre with compost.

organic_remedies.name: Sanitation
organic_remedies.apply: Remove infected leaves and crop residue.

dis_leaf_spot.chemical_comparison: Protective fungicides need frequent repeats in wet weather and wash off into water bodies.

dis_rust.name: Rust

organic_remedies.name: Wettable sulphur spray
organic_remedies.timing: At first pustules, repeat after 10 days

organic_remedies.name: Resistant / early varieties
organic_remedies.apply: Choose local rust-resistant seed from KVK.

dis_rust.chemical_comparison: Triazole fungicides are effective but repeated use erodes efficacy and harms beneficial fungi.
